conversation.message: How have you been feeling lately, overall?
Pretty good, mostly. Just a bit tired here and there, but that's just work and stuff. I'm managing.
How has that tiredness been affecting the things you usually enjoy?
Not too much, really. I still like to go out with friends, but I might just sit out a bit more if we stay out late.
Is it harder to focus or concentrate than it used to be?
Sometimes, yeah. I'll be doing a task and just zone out for a second, but I snap back pretty quick.
How often does that zoning out happen during a typical day?
Not that often, maybe once or twice. It’s not like it’s a constant thing or anything.
How have you been sleeping lately?
Pretty good, mostly. I get a full night’s sleep, so I don’t think it’s the sleep itself.
What makes you say it's not the sleep itself?
I wake up feeling rested, so I don't think it's a problem.
Been doing anything you enjoy lately?
Yeah, I picked up a guitar recently, so I've been playing that a bit. It’s been nice to have something new to focus on.
What's it been like to have something new to focus your mind on?
It’s been really good, actually. It takes my mind off work and I enjoy it, so it’s been a nice change.
When you think about the next few weeks, what do you expect day to day?
More of the same, probably. Just trying to stay on top of things and maybe get a bit more organized.
What does "more of the same" look like for you on a typical day?
Just work, chores, that sort of thing. Nothing too exciting, but it’s all manageable.
Do you find it harder to make decisions than before, even small ones?
Not really. I can still make decisions, it’s just that sometimes I feel like I’m dragging my feet a bit.
Can you tell me more about what "dragging your feet" feels like for you?
It’s just a bit of a hesitation, like I’m not sure what to do with my hands. It goes away once I actually start doing something.
Do you feel like you have enough energy for your usual day?
I have enough energy to get through the day, but I might be a bit more tired than I used to be.
How long have you been feeling more tired than usual?
A few months, I think. It’s not a huge deal, just a bit of a adjustment.
Are you still into the things you used to care about?
Yeah, I still like the same hobbies and stuff. It’s just work that’s a bit more draining than it used to be.
What about work makes it feel more draining to you now?
Just the workload, I guess. There’s a lot on my plate, so it feels like I’m constantly running to keep up.
Is there anything weighing on your mind that you wish you could change?
Not really. I mean, work can be a bit stressful sometimes, but it’s manageable.
What about the stress at work—does it ever leave you feeling down on yourself?
Not really. I know I’m doing okay, so I don’t let it get to me.
How do you feel about how things have gone for you recently?
I think I’m doing alright. I might be a bit tired, but I’m managing.
What's been making you feel like you have to just manage lately?
Just work being a bit more demanding than it used to be.
How's your appetite been?
It's been fine, I think. I eat, so I'm not going hungry or anything.
Have you noticed any change in how much you're eating compared to usual?
Not really. I still eat the same amount, so I don't think it's affecting my diet.
When you say this will end soon, are you talking about ending your life?
No, I mean work. It will slow down eventually, and I'll have more time for myself.
Have you thought about specific steps or a specific way you would do it?
No, I haven't really thought about it that much.
Do you currently have access to what you would use?
No, I don't think so.
What has stopped you so far from acting on these thoughts?
Just common sense, I guess.
You said this might happen soon - what has made things feel this immediate right now?
Just work being a bit more stressful than usual.
Have you found yourself getting emotional more easily lately?
No, not really. I might get a bit snappy sometimes, but I usually snap back pretty quick.
What usually happens right before you feel that snap coming on?
I don’t know, maybe just a lot of noise or something.
When you need to choose, do you get stuck or go back and forth?
Sometimes I go back and forth, but I usually just make a decision and move on.
When you do go back and forth, how long does that typically last?
Just a few minutes. I don’t waste too much time on it.
Do you feel physically restless or on edge in your body?
Not really. I might get a bit fidgety, but I usually just get up and move around to fix it.
How often do you find yourself needing to get up and move around like that?
Not too often, just occasionally.
Is it worse when you have to sit still or wait?
Maybe a bit. If I have to sit around doing nothing, I get a bit bored and restless.
When you feel that restlessness, do you notice any physical sensations that come with it?
Not really. I might just get a bit of a headache or feel a bit tired, but it’s not a specific sensation.
Does even a simple choice feel like too much sometimes?
Not really. I can usually make a decision, even if it takes a few minutes.
When you do take those few minutes to decide, what's going through your mind?
Just weighing the pros and cons, I guess. It’s not a big deal.
Is it more 'heavy and slow' or 'drained after little effort'?
It’s probably more heavy and slow.
How long does that heaviness usually last?
Just a few minutes. It goes away once I actually start doing something.
Does rest actually help, or are you still flat afterward?
Rest usually helps. I just need a bit of sleep.
